task: T3: add the applyable-patch writer to scripts/ralph-log.sh. Define `log_patch <task-label> <attempt>` writing `log_path "$1" "$2" patch`. Build it as `git -C "${ROOT:-.}" add -A -N -- . ':!.evidence'` followed by `git -C "${ROOT:-.}" diff -- . ':!.evidence'` — the intent-to-add pass is what makes NEW files appear in a diff at all, and without it a task whose deliverable is a new file produces an empty patch that `git apply --check` still accepts, which is a false green. Both commands must carry the `':!.evidence'` pathspec so the harness's own record never enters the patch. `-N` records intent only and must leave the real `git add -A` that follows it in the loop unaffected. Same LOG_OK guard, same `|| true`. No call site.
